visual.general_description: Single color endoscopic still of the bowel lumen with diffusely red-orange, granular-looking mucosa.
visual.detailed_description: Octagonal endoscopic field with black corners and no text, arrows, panel letters or scale. A rounded luminal opening sits left of centre and curves away to a darker, bent segment at the upper centre. The surrounding wall is diffusely orange-red (erythematous) with a fine granular/nodular surface texture and many small bright white specks, likely specular light reflections or tiny exudate/bubbles. A few short, thin dark-red linear marks lie right of the lumen and near the upper right edge, and a patchy whitish-yellow area is present at the right/lower right of the wall. No branching submucosal vascular pattern is distinguishable at this resolution, and no discrete, well-delineated ulcer crater is clearly outlined. No instrument or scope landmark that would identify the bowel segment is visible.

visual.general_description: Round field of pink- and purple-stained liver tissue under the microscope with a yellow oval drawn over the central parenchyma.
visual.detailed_description: Circular microscope field (black corners, cream background) with no text, scale bar, stain or magnification label. A strip of pink eosinophilic tissue with purple round nuclei runs diagonally from lower left to upper right; hepatocytes are arranged in plates/cords with small clear sinusoidal spaces. A bright yellow-orange hand-drawn-style oval annotation, not explained in the caption, encloses a central area where the parenchyma looks more crowded and disordered with scattered small dark nuclei and some denser pink cells. Below the oval, an empty white lumen (vessel/duct-like space) is edged by a cluster of small round dark-purple nuclei forming a periportal-type cellular aggregate; smaller dark nuclei are also scattered between hepatocytes. Edges of the section at the right and lower right abut blank background. Fine features such as interface activity, individual necrotic hepatocytes, fibrosis or plasma cells cannot be resolved at this magnification and resolution.
